My two mu is small, just me at home. My son does not farm. I have been doing wheat and maize fifty years, same as everyone in the village. I do what I did last year — it worked, the grain filled, no reason to change.

For wheat in October, I plough once with the rotary, then sow. I buy one bag compound fertilizer (50 jin, the 15-15-15) and half a bag of erming (二铵) for the base — dump it before sowing. The seed I get from the shop in town, the improved kind everybody buys, maybe Jimai. Two mu, so about 30 jin seed per mu. After winter, when the wheat turns green in spring, I spread about 25 jin urea per mu, and again a little at jointing if the leaves look yellow. Better to give a little extra — if the wheat is hungry the harvest is thin and I lose money, but a bit more urea costs only a few yuan. I water four times from my well: one before the ground freezes, one in spring green-up, one at jointing, one when the grain fills. Spray once for weeds, once for the aphids and rust when I see them.

For maize after wheat in June, no plough, just sow into the stubble with the seeder the neighbor rents out. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the shop pushes that year. One bag compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, then 30 jin urea per mu at big trumpet stage. Maize drinks a lot — I water once or twice if the rain is short. Spray once for borer, once for weeds.

I do not measure close. I go by the bag. One bag here, half bag there. Same as my neighbors on both sides. If their maize stands tall, mine should too.
